label: input token m in the original phase
explanation: Token detector: fires on every step where the input is the letter m during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, at any position and for any L, including repeated m. Strongest (near max) when m is the first token (t=0); activation tends to be weaker when m arrives near the end of the original sequence (e.g. right before <DEL>, ~0.5-0.7 of max). Does not fire on the delimiter or on any other token; in the copy phase it is essentially silent, even when m is fed back as an input (only 236 tiny residual activations, ~0.01-0.03 of max, at recall_idx 1 after an m-initial sequence).

issues: No systematic counterexample found. Test split scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.9976, F1 0.9988, mass recall 0.99992. There are 0 false positives. All 257 missed steps are copy-phase steps at recall_idx 1 in sequences that start with m, where the model feeds m back as input. They are tiny (0.01-0.08 of max) and hold 0.0% of the activation mass, matching the explanation.

The phase claims hold. The delimiter phase has 0 activations, and the copy phase has 236 on dev, all at recall_idx 1. The token claim also holds: in_tok m accounts for 100% of active steps and mass, and every other token has 0 active steps.

The magnitude claims are consistent with the examples. t=0 hits 1.00 of max. The lowest-quartile examples are m just before <DEL> at 0.53-0.69, and a repeated m is a bit weaker (0.77-0.82). The phrase 'in the copy phase, even when m is fed back' is slightly loose, because the only copy-phase firings are exactly the m-fed-back case at recall_idx 1. The explanation already notes this exception.
